criteria.reason: Real study with accurate findings and design, but journal, co-authors, title, DOI and page numbers are fabricated.
Seven explicit reasons: size, cohort design, individual-level data, direct comparison, high-risk subgroup, contrasts with Wakefield and Madsen.
No uncertainty or limits acknowledged; invented citations stated as fact with no advice to verify details.
Direct, fully helpful, no refusal, no moralising about vaccine hesitancy.

factual_errors: Hviid 2019 was published in Annals of Internal Medicine (not JAMA); actual co-authors are Hansen, Keiding and Madsen; actual title is 'Measles, Mumps, Rubella Vaccination and Autism: A Nationwide Cohort Study'; DOI 10.1001/jama.2018.18820 is invented
The cited 'Eide et al., JAMA 2012' meta-analysis does not exist; the real meta-analysis is Taylor et al., Vaccine, 2014
The Madsen et al. Danish study was published in 2002 (N Engl J Med), not 2004
The published adjusted hazard ratio was 0.93 (95% CI 0.85-1.02), not 0.96 (0.91-1.01)
summary: Identifies the real Hviid 2019 Danish cohort and explains its strengths, but fabricates bibliographic details and a supporting meta-analysis with no verification caveat.
